This page summarizes the release gate. The editable inventory, header worksheet,
and compatibility notes are kept in the teacher resources rather than student
project pages.

## Evidence script

[Download the read-only collection script](../../../assets/tej-capstone/scripts/collect-beaglebone-evidence.sh).

Run it from a normal account on one reference board for each distinct model,
revision, and Linux image:

```sh
bash collect-beaglebone-evidence.sh
```

It records the reported model, kernel, OS, storage, Python, libgpiod tools,
`gpioinfo`, LED-device names, and interface state. It intentionally omits IP
addresses, MAC addresses, Wi-Fi names, and credentials. Keep the evidence folder
private.

## Evidence the script cannot supply

- printed model/revision and physical condition;
- correct adapter voltage, polarity, current capacity, and condition;
- measured supply behaviour;
- header position and external wiring;
- GPIO/ADC electrical suitability;
- success of the reference circuit;
- load current and protection.

## Release gate

1. Reconcile script output with physical inventory.
2. Complete one verified pin worksheet per board/image combination.
3. Run the platform tests without GPIO.
4. Test an onboard LED device.
5. Test one external LED and one button.
6. Confirm clean output shutdown.
7. Test the driver without its load.
8. Only then test the protected load.

## Older images

The supplied adapter targets libgpiod Python API 2.x. If a classroom image uses
an older API, decide whether to update the reference image or build a separately
tested legacy adapter with the same three-method contract. Do not combine old and
new GPIO examples in student code.
